text:
ops-bot: ALERT south2-dedicated control-plane -> detected netlink peering flaps between rack-a and rack-b; scheduler reporting growing pending queue for GPU pods and ~12 nodes Unready. Auto-evacuation not triggered yet, tagging for ops. :warning:
alex: Seeing BGP session resets + kubelet node condition spikes. Logs:```May 03 03:21:12 node-a kernel: netlink: peer reset
kubelet[1]: I0503 03:21:15.123456  1234 status_manager.go:xxx NodeCondition NetworkUnavailable=true
```Nodes reachable for SSH but pod networking intermittent.
maya: Ok. Proposing immediate traffic shift for low-priority orgs in south2 to hosted so we don't backpressure customer queues. Suggest hosted_weight for tier=low -> 0.8 (was 0.2). No changes for reserved/committed orgs. Any objections? :eyes: 
sam: We must keep reserved capacity protected. Add routing exception: reserved_capacity=true => bypass hosted shift. Also add a QoS throttle for non-critical requests (max_concurrent=50/org) to prevent hosted overload.
alex: I can apply the weight change. Curl payload I'll run from ops bastion:```curl -X POST https://config.internal/api/v1/routing/weights -H 'Authorization: Bearer ****' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"region":"south2","tier":"low","hosted_weight":0.8,"exempt_label":"reserved_capacity"}'```
deploy-bot: routing-weight-update job queued: id=rw-1975023333-01, started by alex.
irene: Monitoring update: after initial weight change queue depth for low-priority down ~60%, but hosted cost burn rate estimate up ~$1.2k/day. Also slight latency tail increase on large-model endpoints (95p +80ms). Do we accept temporary cost/latency?
maya: Yes, temporary. We'll enable prefix/KV caching on the hosted edge for south2-origin traffic to reduce token spend and tail latency. Config snippet to flip:```PATCH /api/v1/proxy/cache
{ "region":"south2","enable_kv_cache":true, "cache_ttl_seconds":3600 }```
liz: Add warmup to avoid cold KV caches: warmup job to ping top-10 org model endpoints 1req/60s for 15min rollouts while traffic is moving. Also set model_warmup=true in deploy metadata.
alex: Warmup scheduled (job id warmup-1975023333-01). Also enabled a 10% canary for latency-sensitive orgs to verify no regressions before full shift.
sam: I'll notify Support + CS with a short status note: "south2 dedicated experiencing netlink peering issues; low-priority traffic being routed to hosted; committed customers not affected. Investigating." Drafting now.
maya: Filing incident as Sev2. ops-bot, please create incident ticket and add oncall.
ops-bot: Incident created INC-20260503-1975; oncall=maya; priority=P2; runbook link: https://internal/pager/incidents/INC-20260503-1975. Added watcher group: #eng-infra, #support.
alex: Next steps: keep weights until netlink stability >30m; if more nodes turn Unready, escalate to data-center networking and consider forced node-drain + replace by spare pools.
irene: I'll keep cost/latency dashboards on 1-min refresh and post updates here every 10m.
maya: Thanks all — keep threads short and post critical metric screenshots only. Will coordinate with DC networking for root cause. :thumbsup:
